turns.content: ok so, when does a pattern stop being just accidents. like, missing a celiac thing over and over. leaving someone off the family chat repeatedly. at what point is it not just oversights anymore.

It stops being “just accidents” when the *information* has already landed and the *system* never changes.

One miss is human. Brains drop balls. The shift is when all of this is true at once:

**They already know.** You’ve said the celiac thing. You’ve said the chat. It’s not new data.

**It keeps happening to the same need / same person.** Accidents scatter. Patterns cluster. If the “oops” always costs *you* and almost never costs them, that’s not randomness.

**They remember comparable stuff.** They don’t forget the group dinner, the flight, the in-joke, the thing *they* care about. Memory is often a priority list wearing a forgetfulness costume.

**There’s no repair that actually repairs.** A real accident gets a specific apology *and* a new habit: a note in the reservation, you added to the chat as an admin, a checklist, a “wait—did we include X?” pause. “Sorry, I forgot” with zero change is just the same event with better manners.

**You have to keep re-explaining.** Once is a reminder. Twice is a nudge. After that, you’re doing unpaid project management for your own inclusion. That’s the tell.

Intent is the wrong courtroom a lot of the time. It doesn’t have to be “they sat down and decided to hurt you.” It can be: you’re not in the default picture. Your need is optional. The group’s convenience outranks your safety or belonging. That’s not a villain monologue. It’s still not an accident.

A useful line:

- **Accident:** rare, uncorrelated, shrinks after feedback.
- **Pattern:** repeats after they know, same direction every time, no new system.
- **Choice (even a lazy one):** they could have built a 10-second safeguard and didn’t, because the cost of forgetting sits on you.

Celiac is the sharper one. That’s not “I forgot your vibe.” After they’ve been told, serving gluten anyway is treating a medical constraint like a preference they can shrug. Family chat is the belonging version of the same move: you exist when someone happens to remember you.

You don’t need a confession to trust the data. If you’ve named it clearly more than once and nothing in their *behavior* updates, you’re allowed to stop calling it an oversight and start calling it how they rank you. Then the question isn’t “was it on purpose?” It’s “do I keep paying the tax for their forgetfulness?”

**Statement**

Her exclusion of me is not an accident. It is intentional.

She has been told, more than once, what I need and that I am part of this family. She has still left me out of the family chat. She has still ignored my celiac restriction. Those are not one-off slips. They are a pattern that continued after she already knew.

Once someone has the information and nothing in their behavior changes, it is no longer an oversight. It is a choice. She is choosing not to include me. She is choosing not to treat my health as real. The cost of that choice keeps landing on me.

I am done calling this forgetfulness. Her exclusion of me is intentional, and I need Marcus and this family to name it that way and stop protecting it as a misunderstanding.
